question: Can discrete convexity of the exact current cost reduce logical failure to one connected unit-current path, yielding a positive path partition bound on the physical Bayes LER without replica continuation?
hypotheses: When (1-p)^2 >= p^2 q(1-q), a logically wrong maximum-weight current implies a simple boundary-to-boundary unit shift from the true current with likelihood ratio at least one. Conformal flow decomposition and discrete convexity supply the proof.

The fixed-path witness probability depends only on counts of forward/backward steps and can be evaluated as a finite binomial sum. Summing paths bounds physical Bayes LER because current-MAP is an admissible charge-only rule.

At q=1,p<=1/2, minimizing occupied count then right-boundary current removes the second path orientation. A positive oriented-path partition function bounds LER and reproduces the known directed dilute coefficient.
A half-Chernoff bound gives a link fugacity gamma=sqrt(p(1-p))*(sqrt(q)+sqrt(1-q)); 3 gamma<1 supplies a sufficient exponential-correctability region, not the exact threshold.
